chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Ḥabīb al-Khathʿamī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Inform me about voluntary fasting and about these three days: if I become junub at the beginning of the night, and I know that I have become junub, then I deliberately sleep until dawn breaks, should I fast or should I not fast?

key_terms.أَجْنَبْتُ: I entered the state of janābah
key_terms.الثَّلَاثَةِ الْأَيَّامِ: the three recommended days of fasting
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn, the beginning of the fasting day

ai.seo_question: Can a person in a state of janābah until dawn still perform an optional fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about voluntary fasting, including the recommended fasting of three days, for one who remains in a state of janābah until dawn deliberately. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that such a person should still fast, indicating that this state does not invalidate this non-obligatory fast.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1788 - It is narrated by Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Habib al-Khath'ami, who said:
"I said to Abu Abdullah (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)): 'Inform me about optional fasting and about fasting on these three days. If I become in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity) at the beginning of the night and I know that I am in such a state but I deliberately sleep until dawn breaks, should I fast or not?'
Imam (as) said: 'Fast.'"
